page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-48 is an x86_64 server instance engineered for workloads demanding an elevated memory footprint. The configuration provides 48 dedicated virtual processor cores matched with 378.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per allocated vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disks for operating system hosting and data storage needs. Furthermore, c4d-highmem-48 contains no onboard GPU hardware accelerators and is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses.

By providing an approximate 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the server delivers high resource density for memory-bound tasks. This structure offers qualitative operational cost efficiency by providing large memory allocations without compelling users to overprovision CPU core counts. Primary workload fits include in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large relational database engines, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-48 is a high-memory compute instance built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated virtual processor cores and 378.0 GB of system memory, representing a high memory density of roughly 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The instance is unaccelerated, featuring zero bundled GPUs, and does not include local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of external block volumes for storage needs. It is also delivered without default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With an approximate 1:8 core-to-memory balance, c4d-highmem-48 allows organizations to scale large memory requirements without paying for excess compute cores. This profile is engineered for memory-intensive production workloads including in-memory data grids, caching engines, enterprise resource planning backends, and memory-heavy database deployments.
